source: Phase B (Track C) pre-registered results; post hoc sets 1 and 2 (exploratory, seed 11). Numbers generated from the result files by build_results_json.py.

open_set.text: SamsungCamera and Chromecast (never seen by the identity model) claiming each verified device: accepted 0 times; 88% / 56% of windows marked UNCERTAIN / UNKNOWN.

phaseB.h5: Claimed-device input to the detector: +0.047 macro detection (95% CI +0.003 to +0.094); failed the declared rule (needed +0.05 in every seed; seed 11 gave +0.032).
phaseB.h6: Per-device detectors (routing): no gain over the shared detector (-0.003, CI -0.028 to +0.019).

speed: Wrong claims: rejected in the first 15-minute window in 100% of trials. Detector alert after a median of 2 minutes (NetatmoCamera claiming TPLinkPlug never alerted: the identity check is what catches it). Attacks flagged about 2 minutes after they start.

c1.text: Black-box impersonation never got accepted: success 0.000 for naive and adaptive attackers at every bound and query budget (no-attack reference 0.005).

c2a.text: Mislabelled attack minutes cost 6-11 points of detection, mostly on TPLinkPlug and WeMoSwitch. The trimmed refit passes the rule, but recovers nothing against no defence: weak evidence.

c2b.text: Poisoning identity with a partner device's windows: partner acceptance 0.000 at every rate. Label filtering removed 100% of poisoned windows and raised honest acceptance from 0.908 to 0.943 on clean data.

c3.text: 1000/1000 byte flips refused, 100/100 manifest flips, 100/100 signature flips; every substitution refused; malicious pickle refused before loading. Replay of a whole older bundle is accepted unless a version floor is pinned.

trackF.text: Exploratory rolling-origin check over time (4 folds). By the declared rule all four Verified devices are WITHDRAWN: alarm rate exceeded 5% in at least one block (Netatmo 0.996 in fold 2, LIFX 0.095 in fold 5, WeMoSwitch 0.062 in fold 3, TPLinkPlug 0.056 in fold 3). Identity is stable for WeMoSwitch, TPLinkPlug, LIFX; Netatmo is unstable.

routing: Identity-aware routing was tried 5 times and did not beat the plain detector. A wrong claim makes the detector flag 93-95% of benign minutes, so the detector itself is not the identity check. Reported as tried and failed.
limits: Recorded traffic from one lab, two recording periods, scripted attacks. No claim of general IoT security.
Only four devices are claimed, as verified on the Phase B test days. Track F (over time) did not show them stable: thresholds drift and would need recalibration.
Small attack counts: 100% detection is compatible with a true rate as low as about 65-77% per device (95% interval).

Behaviour cannot tell a perfect clone from the real device. Partial clones (up to 90% copied) are mostly rejected; a perfect copy is accepted. Device attestation (a key on the device) is needed for that case.
A volume threshold matches the autoencoder on two of the four verified devices; the autoencoder adds most on TPLinkPlug and LIFX.
Impersonation was tested with a constant add-only black-box attacker; stronger attackers were not tested.
The signed bundle does not cover poisoning before signing or theft of the signing key.
Post hoc numbers are exploratory, seed 11, on test data that had already been opened.
